diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Mahmoud Nabavian, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, called for a review of the composition of the negotiation team with the United States. He asked Mohsen Rezaei on the social network X to reconsider the members of the negotiation team in the current sensitive conditions. Nabavian referred to the failed experiences of negotiations with the US and said that former members are also present in the ongoing negotiations.

Iraj Mesdaghi, a political analyst, said the focus of the struggle is the freedom of Iran and opposition to the Islamic Republic, not divisions among Iranians. He added that Prince Reza Pahlavi considers himself the trustee of an award that is to be given to the brave people of Iran and has extended a hand of friendship to all Iranians, both supporters and critics.

Vahid Sarlak, an athlete, after the 2026 Friedrich Naumann Foundation Freedom Award ceremony, considered the main message of the event to be unity among the people of Iran. He said the award was given to the people of Iran and the youth who are fighting for freedom. Sarlak added that the final decision-maker about Iran's fate is the people of Iran, not Berlin, Washington, or any other capital.

Amir Shahidi-Nejad, father of Mehrshad Shahidi-Nejad, was sentenced to two years and six months suspended imprisonment and a fine instead of two years and six months of actual imprisonment. Mehrshad Shahidi-Nejad was killed during the "Woman, Life, Freedom" protests in 1401. Amir Shahidi-Nejad had previously criticized the judicial process.

Reports have emerged about explosions in Isfahan that were later announced as "controlled explosions of unexploded ammunition in the south and north of Isfahan." These explosions were heard at various times on the morning of Saturday, 16 Aban [2026-11-07], causing shaking of windows and the ground. Additionally, sounds of explosions were reported in Shiraz, which had been announced beforehand.

Contrary to Iran's international commitments under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and obligations regarding the non-use of children in military affairs, 37 female high school students from Buin Miandasht county were sent to operational areas in the south of the country as part of the so-called "Rahian-e Noor" tours. Also, a Rahian-e Noor camp official in Golestan province announced that 1,000 male students and 1,000 female students from the counties of Maraveh Tappeh, Gomishan, Bandar-e Gaz, and Aq Qala will be sent to operational areas.

In Frankfurt, a wall has been erected in memory of Iran's martyrs, especially the victims of the bloody suppression on the 18th and 19th of Dey. Sosha Makani told Iran International that Iranians had a large presence at this gathering and emphasized that wherever Prince Reza Pahlavi is, they are also present. He added that they are striving for the victory of the final battle and the freedom of Iran so that the blood of the martyrs is not in vain.
A video received by Iran International shows a gathering of Iranians in Frankfurt after the Freedom Award was given to Prince Reza Pahlavi.

Hossein Mohseni, spokesperson for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, announced on Saturday, 16 Aban, in a press conference that the range limitations of Iran's missiles have been lifted. He warned that if a new round of conflicts with the US and Israel begins, the IRGC Aerospace Force will deploy weapons and capabilities that will surprise the world. Mohseni added that these capabilities must be demonstrated in practice and mere slogans are not enough.
The head of the judiciary in Bam county reported the execution of a prisoner previously sentenced to death for the murder of his wife.

A video sent by a viewer to Iran International shows that on Saturday, simultaneously with the awarding of the Friedrich Naumann Foundation Freedom Prize in Germany, a memorial wall was erected for the martyrs of the Iranian National Revolution.

Borzo Arjmand said in an interview with Iran International that all Iranians abroad try to be the voice of the Iranian people and inform governments about events in Iran. He stated that 99% of artists inside Iran oppose the Islamic Republic and added that they shout abroad instead of the artists inside and will succeed.
According to videos received by Iran International, Iranians participating in the Frankfurt gathering, which took place after awarding a prize to Prince Reza Pahlavi, shouted "Long live the Shah."

The Iraqi Foreign Minister said on Saturday, 16 Aban, that the current situation indicates the possibility of a renewed war in the region, and the US has officially asked Baghdad to close all its border crossings with Iran except for two. He said Baghdad has informed Tehran that it accepts friendship and alliance with Iran but does not accept the Islamic Republic's interference in Iraq's internal affairs. He also announced ongoing negotiations with the Najba Movement and Kata'ib Hezbollah regarding weapons and said Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq and Kata'ib Sayyid al-Shuhada have agreed to control their weapons.

Ali Zaghi and Ilya Akbari, two detainees from the January 1404 protests, were sentenced to death by the Mashhad Revolutionary Court. They were tried in a joint case called 'Shandiz' along with four others. The charges include waging war through participation in destruction of public property and setting fire to religious centers.

Masoumeh Taherkhani, an economic analyst, said that the transfer of sanctions from Asia to Canada shows that the US aims to limit the financial routes of the Islamic Republic worldwide. She added that cryptocurrency networks and transfers of Tether and Bitcoin are also traceable, and these measures increase the cost and difficulty for the Islamic Republic to circumvent sanctions.

Ali Zaghi and Ilya Akbari, two detainees of the Iranian National Revolution in Dey 1404, were sentenced to death in the case known as "Shandiz." According to Harana, the charges against these six prisoners include "waging war through participation in the destruction of public property and burning religious centers" and "assembly and collusion against national security." The death sentences of Mehdi Zarif and Hossein Rasouli-Nasab have been confirmed, while the sentences of Ali Zaghi, Ilya Akbari, Matin Shabani, and Hassan Golshan-Nejad are at the preliminary stage.

Esteghlal football team was held to a 2-2 draw against Esteghlal Khuzestan in Ahvaz in the 12th week of the Premier League. Saleh Hardani scored in minutes 65 and 90+12 for Esteghlal, while Seyed Mehdi Mousavi in minute 88 and Aref Rostami in minute 90+5 scored for Esteghlal Khuzestan. The match saw two red cards for Esteghlal Tehran, and Aref Rostami missed a penalty kick for Esteghlal Khuzestan in minute 45+1.

Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, wrote to US officials: "Start a war, you will face a devastating response." Rezaei, on Saturday, November 7, 2026, in an English message on the X network, called the US the loser of the war and elections and asked: "So exactly to whom in Washington should we deliver this message?"

Darya Safaei, an Iranian-descendant member of the Belgian Parliament, said the gathering of Iranians in Frankfurt shows that the people of Iran are determined to reclaim their country and the day of victory is very near. She added that the view of European statesmen towards the Islamic Republic has changed and they no longer want to appease this regime.

Elahe Tavakolian, an eye injury victim of the 1401 protests, said this award is for the families of the deceased and victims of repression. She hopes that one day this award will be presented to the families of the immortal and the injured in Azadi Square.

Forough Kenani, a sociology researcher and women's rights activist, said at an Iranian gathering in Frankfurt that the balance of power must shift in favor of the people. She added that every step taken brings the people of Iran one step closer to a free tomorrow.

The Qatari newspaper Al-Araby Al-Jadeed reported that the Prime Minister of Iraq has ordered security commanders to prevent any suspicious movements of armed groups. This order was issued after receiving information about unusual movements of two armed groups.
The Tehran prosecutor summoned a former manager of IRIB following his recent statements. Domestic media identified this person as Hassan Rouzitalab, former director of political programs at IRIB.

Prince Reza Pahlavi said on Saturday, 16 Aban, at an Iranian gathering in Frankfurt that only the free vote of the people at the ballot box will determine Iran's future, and Iranians must remain united to achieve the right to choose and end the Islamic Republic. After receiving the 2026 Friedrich Naumann Foundation Freedom Award, he said the medal belongs to the Iranian people and that the presence of Iranians at this gathering is an example of their unity. He added that the Iranian people want the freedom and human rights enjoyed by people in free countries.

Abdolnaser Hemmati, the governor of the Central Bank, said that about 30 billion dollars of currency have been provided for imports in the first seven months and 15 days of the year, and there is no shortage in the supply of essential goods. He added that the supply of raw materials for production and medicine continues. Hemmati also said that more than 9,000 trillion rials of credit have been paid, 75% of which has been allocated to businesses and a large part to working capital.

Three workers died in work accidents in Mashhad and Hamedan. Two of them died in Mashhad while working with a shredder and repairing a heavy vehicle. The third, a guard of a half-finished building in Hamedan, died from carbon monoxide poisoning.

A video sent to Iran International shows a group of Iranians living in Spain on Saturday, 16 Aban, displaying images of martyrs in Madrid in support of Prince Reza Pahlavi and to recall the killing of people during the national revolution.

Political analyst Nejat Bahrami said the widespread presence of Iranians at the Frankfurt rally indicates that the protest movement against the Islamic Republic is no longer dependent on sporadic events, and support for the leadership of Prince Reza Pahlavi has continued. According to him, such rallies can influence the decisions of hesitant Western politicians and amplify the voice of protesters inside Iran. Bahrami added that cooperation among various factions is essential to transform this social support into effective political action.

Reza Talebi, a journalist, said Russia has used military cooperation with the Islamic Republic to advance its interests and tries to maintain the balance of power between Tehran and Washington. He added that Donald Trump probably seeks to use Russia's influence over the Islamic Republic to bring Tehran back to the negotiating table and secure the Strait of Hormuz. Talebi emphasized that there are serious doubts about Moscow's sincerity in mediation.

Companions of a patient clashed with a physician on duty at Dehgolan Hospital last night and assaulted him. The physician was injured, and the conflict ended with police intervention. The patient's companions continued their threats, and the physician is concerned about returning to the hospital.
A death row inmate in Khorramabad was saved from execution after 18 years, following the forgiveness of the victims' next of kin in a family dispute.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, called for the formation of a national unity government and said such a government would permanently eliminate the nuclear threat from the Islamic Republic and lead to internal unity. He warned that a government involving supporters of terrorism and Islamists would not address the threat from the Islamic Republic and would lead to Israel's internal collapse. Netanyahu described the formation of a national unity government as essential for the country's survival.
Tensions between Iran and the US continue. Trump's cabinet and advisors have commented on the possibility of an attack. Details of their statements are included in the report.
In the audio version of Titrawal with Niusha Saremi, it was reported that the Freedom Award was given to Prince Reza Pahlavi. It was also reported that thousands of Iranians gathered in Frankfurt.

In recent weeks, a group of government supporters named 'Tavva' have gathered in front of military institutions including the army and the Revolutionary Guards, chanting slogans against them and accusing them of negligence. Some media close to the Revolutionary Guards wrote that members of this group are close to Saeed Jalili.

Workers of the contracting company Kondovan Pars in Chabahar reported that they have not been paid for more than four months. According to one of these workers, several of their colleagues who went on strike on Thursday, 14 Aban, for their demands were dismissed by the company management.

Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, President of Turkey, said in a phone call with Donald Trump that tensions between the Islamic Republic and the US must end and disputes should be resolved through diplomacy. Ankara continues its efforts to establish peace. Erdoğan also expressed hope that increased diplomatic efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war will be fruitful.
It has been reported that there is difficulty in supplying 40 essential and vital medicines. An interview was conducted with Babak Khatti, a pediatrician and specialist.

Yaser Asani, Esteghlal star, was sent off in the final minutes of the match against Esteghlal Khuzestan after an altercation with the assistant referee. Broadcast images show he made a move similar to Shoja Khalilzadeh's verbal confrontation with the referee. This move is known in Iranian football as the "Shoja Groin".

Saeed Fattahi, head of the football organization of Esteghlal Tehran club, said after the match against Esteghlal Khuzestan that the pressures led to Yaser Asani's expulsion. Ozjan Bizati, Esteghlal's coach, blamed the referee for disrupting Asani's focus. Esteghlal club issued a statement demanding an investigation into the events at Ghadir Stadium in Ahvaz.

According to Polish police, an armed person opened fire in the historic center of Krakow, the second largest city in the country, resulting in 6 deaths and about 12 injuries. Police officers shot the suspect who is now in custody. Images shared by users show the suspect and a police officer on the ground and police forces at the scene.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing the production of beer at home simultaneously with the sound of government slogans in the street.

Isaac Herzog, President of Israel, announced on the evening of Saturday, 16 Aban, that he will assign the mission of forming the government to Gadi Eizenkot, head of the Yashar party. Herzog had said that factions with a total of 67 seats support Eizenkot, but it is still unclear who can form the government. Benjamin Netanyahu said some intend to form a government with the participation of "supporters of terrorism," and such a government would not confront the threat of the Islamic Republic.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International on Saturday, 16 Aban [Gregorian: 2026-11-07], writing the word "Bibi" on the fogged glass of his car as a sign of Benjamin Netanyahu, saying: "It is raining and I remember the day of Khamenei's death when the weather had been rainy for several days."
Iran International reported that Putin's influence in Iran will increase after Khamenei's death.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said Russia has tried to keep the Islamic Republic neither strong enough to be independent from Moscow nor weak enough to collapse. He added that Vladimir Putin has so far used Iran's war to serve Russia's interests, especially in the Ukraine issue and the energy sector. Mahdavi-Azad raised the possibility of a change in Russia's role in the war and an expansion of military aid to the Islamic Republic.

A reporter from IRIB reported on Saturday, 16 Aban, that explosion-like sounds were heard in Qeshm, Sirik, Jask, and Bandar Abbas, and the cause of these sounds is still unknown. The reporter suggested these sounds might be related to the actions of the Islamic Republic's armed forces in "defense of the Strait of Hormuz," but gave no further explanation. The reporter said they are waiting for precise information from official sources to clarify the nature of these sounds.

HRA reported that the Revolutionary Court of Mashhad, headed by Hossein Yazdankhah, Ali Zaghi, and Ilya Akbari, sentenced two protesters from Dey 1404 to death. With these sentences, the number of protesters sentenced to death in the case known as "Shandiz" reached six. An interview was conducted with Pegah Bani Hashemi, a legal researcher, about the legal aspects of these sentences and the condition of the convicts.

Donald Trump, President of the United States, announced that he has asked Dana White, a prominent figure in mixed martial arts, to become the White House spokesperson and bring several fighters as his assistants. Trump described White as a "fierce fighter and warrior" and invited 6 current or former UFC champions to join him. He said these individuals are needed to defend against crazy leftists.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said Prince Reza Pahlavi called the Freedom Award a trust until the day of Iran's freedom while receiving it on behalf of the Iranian people. He also emphasized the common points among Iranians to overcome the Islamic Republic both at the award ceremony and among Iranians in Frankfurt.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that Prince Reza Pahlavi, despite his widespread popularity among Iranians, has always emphasized returning to the ballot box to determine Iran's future political system. He added that Reza Pahlavi sees the institutionalization of democracy as dependent on strengthening civil institutions, party systems, free elections, and media freedom.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported on Saturday an incident between a bulk carrier and military forces in the Sea of Oman, about 18 nautical miles east of Khorfakkan in the United Arab Emirates. The organization stated that there is still no information about the crew's condition, the extent of damage, or possible environmental consequences of the incident.

Joe Wilson, a Republican member of the US House of Representatives, wrote on the social network X: "I deeply thank Syria for its brave leadership in providing military aid to the people of Yemen and Saudi Arabia in the fight against extremist Houthi terrorists." He added: "Syria has been freed from Iran and will soon help liberate Yemen from Iran's domination." The US congressman called for all people in the region to "take action against Iran and its proxy forces."

Afrah Al-Zouba, the Foreign Minister of Yemen's legitimate government, in a message on the social network X, reposted the recent statement of the Lebanese government about the necessity to prevent Lebanese groups from interfering in the internal affairs of Yemen and other Arab countries. She wrote that the governments of Yemen and Lebanon continue their cooperation to confront Hezbollah's support for the Houthis.

Alireza Namvar Haghighi said Gadi Eizenkot, despite parliamentary support for forming the Israeli government, faces serious disagreements among his allies, especially over cooperation with Arab parties. He added that the joint opposition of these parties to Benjamin Netanyahu's continued premiership may help form the government but does not guarantee its stability. Namvar Haghighi identified the main difference between Eizenkot and Netanyahu as their approach to the Islamic Republic, saying Eizenkot considers confronting Tehran's nuclear and missile threats necessary but does not see regime change in Iran as Israel's duty.

Hamed Kavianpour, former Persepolis player and current technical director of the club's academy, said in a video interview that Mr. Karim is not a mourner of Persepolis' losses. Persepolis club announced that by order of the CEO, Kavianpour has been summoned to the disciplinary committee to provide explanations, and a decision will be made about him afterward.

Ali Rashid Al Nuaimi, head of the Defense, Homeland, and Foreign Affairs Committee of the UAE Federal National Council, told Fox News that despite concerns about the potential resumption of military conflict in the Middle East, he has cautious optimism about the Washington-Tehran negotiations. He attributed this optimism to recent progress mediated by Qatar and expressed hope that both sides can build trust and prevent war. Al Nuaimi added that they are planning for the worst-case scenarios while hoping for the best outcome.

Ali Al-Zaidi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, announced that he will not allow groups opposing the state's monopoly on weapons to continue seizing lands and violating the rights of Iraqi citizens. He said these groups use titles and religious justifications to appropriate the rights of others.

Polish authorities announced that an armed man killed six people on Saturday, 16 Aban, in the main square of Krakow and was arrested after a police shooting. Three other bodies were also found in the suspect's home. The Polish interior minister said initial evidence suggests the attacker may have been influenced by far-right ideology, but his motive is still unknown.

Amir Hamidi, a national security expert, pointed to rising tensions in southern Iran and reports of an explosion in Qeshm, saying the risk of escalation has increased. He emphasized that CENTCOM's focus on Caspian Sea routes and land borders could make it harder to transfer weapons and military parts from Russia and China to the Islamic Republic. According to Hamidi, the main goal of these pressures should be to cut the financial and logistical lifeline of the IRGC and limit the Islamic Republic's ability to replace parts and replenish military stockpiles.

Hossein Shariatmadari wrote in a note that there is undeniable evidence showing that the challenge of hijab and chastity is one of the enemy's tools in the upcoming war. He accused the enemy of using unveiling as a destructive weapon and considered neglecting this issue as an involuntary cooperation with the enemy. Shariatmadari also criticized some officials who believe that confronting unveiling during wartime is not expedient.

Ali Mamouri, a political science researcher, said Tehran has moved away from the policy of limiting missile range to within two thousand kilometers. He added that the Islamic Republic, by raising the possibility of targeting US bases in Eastern Europe and considering withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, is reviewing its military and security doctrine.
Iraqi security forces seized a truck carrying 35 missiles and arrested three members of an armed group affiliated with the Islamic Republic.

The Judiciary of the Islamic Republic announced that the death sentences of Hassan Diyuband, Hamid Kazemi, and Reza Zangeneh, three detainees from the protests on 18 and 19 Dey in Karaj, have been carried out after confirmation by the Supreme Court. These individuals were sentenced to death and asset confiscation on charges of participating in operational actions for Israel, the USA, and hostile groups against national security and interests. Additionally, the Revolutionary Court of Karaj sentenced eight other defendants to five to ten years in prison.

Tasnim News Agency reported that Hossein Kheirandish, a proponent of traditional medicine, has been arrested following a complaint by a private plaintiff and the Medical System Organization. Kheirandish had deceived students by promising the opportunity to study for a PhD at a reputable university in Armenia and had received payments in dollars from them. He continued to appear on television programs from 1400 to 1403 and had previously claimed to have performed cupping therapy on Ali Khamenei.

Reuters reported that shortly after the Saudi Civil Defense issued an early warning about a possible threat, several loud explosions were heard in Riyadh. After the explosions were heard, the Saudi Civil Defense announced that the danger in Riyadh had been resolved.

The Victoria and Albert Museum in London is holding a free exhibition of Freddie Mercury's clothes and personal items to mark his 80th birthday. His royal crown and cape are among the eight iconic outfits in the exhibition.

Mohammad Javad Larijani, head of the Institute for Basic Sciences, said that military use of nuclear technology does not necessarily mean building a bomb to kill civilians. He added that military bases can be targeted but attacking civilians or essential infrastructure is not compatible with our principles. Larijani emphasized the need for 80% enrichment and said US bases in Germany, Albania, or Britain would be legitimate targets.

The judiciary announced the execution of Hassan Diyuband, Hamid Kazemi, and Reza Zangeneh, three detainees from the December 1404 protests in Karaj. These sentences were carried out on the morning of Sunday, 17 Aban, after confirmation by the Supreme Court.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said the result of the US elections does not affect the nuclear strategy of the Islamic Republic and any action by the US or Israel will face a severe response. He added that the Islamic Republic will never trade its nuclear industry and changes in US parties do not influence Iran's decisions on war or nuclear issues.

Hakan Fidan, Turkey's foreign minister, called for a global initiative to protect strategic maritime passages and warned that insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz, Bab al-Mandab, and the Black Sea threatens global trade and energy security.

According to reports received by Iran International, Mazkoor Nazari, the father of the disappeared Mehrzad Nazari, died of a stroke on Saturday, 16 Aban. Mehrzad Nazari, 28 years old, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 in Nurabad Mamasani.

Iranian media reported the overturning of a bus carrying players and members of the Sahar Academy women's basketball team on the return route from Abadan to Tehran. Some players and team members were hospitalized in Shoosh and Golestan hospitals in Ahvaz, and the general condition of some is reported to be stable. Other injured individuals remain under medical care.
On the eve of assigning the mission to form a government to Gadi Eisenkot, Benjamin Netanyahu for the first time asked opposition parties to form a national unity government with him.

Alireza Yousefi broke the world record in weightlifting at the World Championships in China by lifting 263 kilograms in the clean and jerk and won the gold medal. He also won the silver medal overall. Ali Davoodi, another Iranian representative in this category, ranked fourth with a total of 452 kilograms.

According to the public relations of Tehran refinery, the cause of the thick smoke observed at this refinery on the morning of Sunday, 17 Aban was due to "electrical and technical problems" and no fire occurred in the refinery units.

The Harana website reported that Abolfazl Sedaghat, a 20-year-old protesting youth, one of the three detainees of the January 2026 protests in Mashhad, has been sentenced to death. Previously, the identities of Matin Farnian and Vahid Khodrikhah, two other protesters sentenced to death in this case, had been confirmed. Abolfazl Sedaghat, born in Esfand 1384, along with Matin Farnian and Vahid Khodrikhah, has been sentenced to death by the Fifth Branch of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court on charges of "Moharebeh" (waging war against God).

A video received by Iran International shows flooding in Fereshteh Street in Tehran on Sunday, 17 Aban, after rainfall. The sender of the video says: "Look at the city management, the street has become a pool."

Hossein Mohseni, spokesperson for the IRGC, said the US plan called "Iron Gate" is just wordplay and the US will not be able to use it to impose severe economic pressure to collapse Iran's economy. He also said that while Iranian vessels might be targeted in wartime, Iran will respond several times over. Mohseni added that the US can never achieve the economic blockade it seeks and Iran has prepared measures to maintain relations with neighboring countries.

Ali Shirazi, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Hossein Shariatmadari in Kayhan newspaper is worried about the lifestyle of the Iranian people and the spread of optional hijab. Shirazi added that Shariatmadari considers these social changes part of the war by the US and Israel against the Islamic Republic and has called for immediate action. These concerns arise while the government is facing economic and livelihood crises.

Ehsan Daneshvar, an environmental and energy expert, said that flooding is a natural and predictable phenomenon but repeated surprise indicates weaknesses in infrastructure and flood risk management. He criticized construction in riverbanks and vegetation destruction, emphasizing that the Islamic Republic has trapped the country in a cycle of crisis instead of scientific water resource management.

Saudi Arabia's official news agency reported on Sunday, 17 Aban, citing a source in the country's Ministry of Energy, that one of Aramco's administrative buildings in Riyadh was targeted in an attack and shrapnel hit the building. According to the report, the building suffered limited damage, but no one was killed or injured. Responsible authorities have also begun investigating the incident.
Following floods in Khuzestan province, water reached the village of Chalchelak. At the same time, the Qom River also flooded, and images of rising water in these areas have been published.

A video received by Iran International shows a mourning ceremony for the late Amirhossein Maleki. Amirhossein Maleki was a 20-year-old protester who was arrested in connection with the December 1404 protests in the Malekshahr neighborhood of Isfahan and was executed on the morning of Aban 12, 1405 [Gregorian: 2026-11-03].

Israel Katz, Israel's Defense Minister, said at a ceremony that the country's mission against the Islamic Republic is not yet over. He warned that Iran is trying to resume its efforts to acquire nuclear weapons and is pursuing other serious actions that put Israel at real risk. Katz emphasized the need for unity and the use of the full strength of the Israeli army and the resilience of the people to confront these threats.

According to reports received by Iran International, Mazkour Nazari, the father of the late Mehrzad Nazari, died due to psychological pressure caused by the death of his child. Earlier, videos of his distress at his child's grave had been published.

A 25-year-old man opened fire in Krakow's historic square, killing six and injuring 15. The Polish government has declared two days of national mourning. Police also reported discovering the bodies of three people at the attacker's residence.

Ali Babaei Karnami, head of the parliamentary social commission, said about eight million people suffer from absolute poverty and malnutrition, and up to 50 million people face difficulties in securing basic goods. He added that the income of one person in a family of four must be at least 100 million to have a normal life. Babaei also said the economic conditions of the people are not favorable and individuals must have one or multiple jobs.
Several media outlets in Iran have released a video titled "Rocket fuel test in a school in Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari." In these images, part of the school's ceiling collapses during the test.

On Sunday, 17 Aban, a number of Social Security retirees held a protest gathering and march in front of the Social Security building in Shush county. Their demands include equalizing pensions, increasing payments in line with living costs, removing the Social Security Organization from government monopoly, resolving supplementary insurance issues, and implementing Article 54 of the Social Security Law to receive free medical services.

Israel Katz, Israel's Defense Minister, said their mission against the Islamic Republic is not yet finished. He warned that the Iranian government is seeking to resume efforts to obtain a nuclear bomb and has not abandoned its nuclear ambitions.
Azar Yahoo, a political prisoner, was released from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad on 11 Aban after completing her sentence. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Asieh Amini, a social issues analyst, said the Islamic Republic continues the killing of the Dey month protesters by issuing death sentences, increasing pressure on families, and restricting information about the cases. She pointed out that defendants have been deprived of access to chosen lawyers and forced confessions have been obtained. Charges such as moharebeh have been attributed to actions like setting trash bins on fire or coordinating attendance at protests.
A video sent to Iran International shows a classroom fire at Bandar Mahshahr University on Sunday, 17 Aban.

Today, Sunday, a group of Social Security retirees held a gathering in front of the organization's building in Rasht, demanding an increase in payments in line with inflation, equalization of salaries, removal of Social Security from government monopoly, and resolution of supplementary insurance issues to improve their medical services.

Ali Sadrazadeh, a Middle East analyst, said that although the Houthis are not militarily capable of confronting Saudi Arabia, even limited attacks and minor damages caused by them can affect Saudi Arabia's economy due to symbolic and psychological consequences.

Simultaneously with the formation of a special US task force to expand the economic siege of Iran, the Iraqi Foreign Minister announced the closure of all border crossings of his country with Iran, except for two crossings. The spokesperson of the IRGC called the Iron Gate plan a "play on words." Mahtab Gholizadeh commented on the impact of the new CENTCOM campaign on Iran's imports and exports.
Fouad Qaderi, a citizen from Javanrud, was released from Dizelabad Prison in Kermanshah on Saturday, 16 Aban, after posting bail.

Hossein Taeb, head of the Basij Organization, said that in coordination with the Ministries of Oil and Energy and the Gas Company, they have obtained a list of high consumers and trained 150,000 Basij members as energy helpers to promote energy saving. He added that devoted members will participate in this plan and a drill on energy saving will be conducted. Taeb also said that energy saving can improve people's livelihoods and everyone must make sacrifices.
